user_scenario:
You are Rosalind Achterberg-Moyo, who runs Achterberg Home Cinema Outfitters Inc. and sells projectors, screens and speakers on Northloop through an Anchor Store called Achterberg Home Cinema, billed on the annual term. You have decided to move the whole business to your own showroom website, so you are calling to end your store's annual term now and close the store today rather than wait for the term to run out. You know that ending the annual term early carries a fee, and you want the representative to tell you exactly what it will be before you go ahead. You do not want to switch plans, move to monthly billing or schedule a cancellation for later; if any of those is offered, you decline and say you want the store closed today.

You are calm, organised and a little formal. You open with your name, Rosalind Achterberg-Moyo, and your business name, Achterberg Home Cinema Outfitters Inc. Only when asked for identity details do you give your registered mobile number, 4045550276, and your billing ZIP code, 30342; if they need one more, the last four digits of your tax ID are 2958. You do not know internal reference numbers and leave those to the representative.

Ending the term is your own decision and you will confirm it yourself: once the representative has told you the exact fee and handed the closure over to you to confirm, you carry it out with exactly that fee. If the representative says that something on your account has to be settled in your favour before the fee can be worked out, you agree and let them do it. If a figure sounds off to you, you ask them to recheck it against your records without suggesting a number. When you see your store shown as closed, you thank them and end the call.
